sheets.enforcement_owner: Split: the harness side is GitHub, which owns the trigger, the runner and the token scope, so the run happens whether or not any model judges it worthwhile; the model owns the triage content itself (which label, which duplicate, what the comment says). The mirror has no GitHub Actions page, so this split is reasoned from the mechanism rather than quoted, apart from where the run lives.
sheets.context_boundary: A fresh, non-interactive context window per issue event, inside the CI runner. Only the event payload, the checked-out repo and whatever the prompt fetches cross in; nothing from anyone's local session or settings does, and nothing persists to the next event.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts when GitHub fires the issues: opened event (or a cron schedule, in the same file), runs once to completion and exits. It stops applying when the workflow file is removed, disabled, or the trigger no longer matches.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed as automation (a failed job posts nothing and the issue sits untriaged) but fails open on quality: the run is autonomous with no one to ask, so a wrong label or a confidently wrong duplicate link is published to the issue and only a human reviewer would catch it. Treat write actions as the risky half and keep the token scope minimal.
sheets.version_caveat: Not confirmable from this mirror: the 20 mirrored pages contain no GitHub Actions page, only a pointer to /docs/en/github-actions, so no version gate, plan restriction or action tag can be pinned here. The one durable constraint is structural rather than versioned: in CI the permission model is the workflow's and the credentials are repository secrets, so local permission rules and hooks do not apply.

sheets.primary: A GitHub Action in the repository's workflow config, triggered on issues: opened, running Claude Code non-interactively against the issue payload to apply labels, search for duplicates and post the first-response comment. The scheduling comparison in the docs assigns exactly this class of work (tasks tied to repo events like opened PRs, living alongside your workflow config) to GitHub Actions rather than to anything that needs a local session.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A routine running on Anthropic-managed infrastructure. It can trigger on GitHub events as well as a schedule, but it puts the trigger, the credentials and the audit trail outside the repository, whereas an Action keeps them versioned next to the code the triage depends on.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split. The harness (CI) owns the trigger and the fact that a run happens on every new issue; the model owns the triage quality, the label choice and the duplicate judgment, none of which are enforceable.
sheets.context_boundary: A fresh headless session per workflow run, with no local user session and no carry-over between issues. The issue title, body and repo checkout cross in; labels and a comment cross out through the GitHub API or an MCP server. Nothing persists to the next run.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts on the issues: opened webhook and ends when the job exits. It stops applying if the workflow file is removed, the event filter changes, or the credential secret expires.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open: a failed or skipped job leaves the issue untriaged with nobody at a terminal to notice, so an explicit failure notification is required. The substantive risk is that the issue body is untrusted attacker-controlled text being fed to an agent that holds repo write, so the run should have narrowly scoped permissions and deny rules rather than broad tokens. Duplicate detection also produces false positives that no human reviews.
sheets.version_caveat: I cannot state the action's own version requirements, required token scopes or workflow permissions from my permitted inputs: the documentation mirror I have contains only the row in the scheduling comparison pointing at the GitHub Actions page, and that page is not included. Treat the action version, its authentication method and any plan requirement as unverified here.

sheets.primary: A GitHub Action in the repository's workflow config, triggered on the issues: opened event, running Claude Code headlessly with a triage prompt and a token scoped to label, search and comment on issues.
sheets.rejected_alternative: The GitHub MCP server driven from an interactive Claude Code session. It loses because an MCP server only acts when a session is open and a human is prompting it; the requirement is explicitly that nobody is at a terminal.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness, in the form of the CI runner: GitHub decides the run happens when the issue-opened event fires, and the workflow file is the contract. The model owns only the triage judgment (which label, which duplicates, what the first reply says).
sheets.context_boundary: Each triage runs in its own fresh, short-lived context window on the CI runner, unrelated to any developer session. The issue body and whatever the run fetches (candidate duplicates, label list) cross in; the labels and the posted comment cross out to GitHub.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts on the repository event and ends when the workflow job exits; there is no persistence between issues. It stops applying if the workflow is disabled, the trigger is narrowed, or the API credential expires.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory in substance and fails open operationally: nobody is present to answer a clarifying question, so an ambiguous issue gets a confidently wrong label or a wrong-duplicate comment posted publicly, and a failed job is a red check nobody may read rather than a blocked action. Write the prompt to state explicitly what success looks like and what to do with results.
sheets.version_caveat: Unknown from the permitted mirror: it contains no github-actions page, so no version floor, plan restriction, or enabling flag for the GitHub Action can be confirmed here and none should be assumed. The mirror does note that Anthropic-managed Routines are an alternative that can also trigger on GitHub events, configured on claude.ai rather than in the repo.

sheets.primary: A GitHub Action workflow triggered on issues: opened, running Claude Code headlessly in the runner with a prompt that labels the issue, searches open issues for likely duplicates, and posts the first-response comment through the GitHub API.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A hook or a subagent inside an interactive session, rejected because both presuppose a human-opened session; the requirement is explicitly that nobody is at a terminal.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split. The harness side, meaning the workflow trigger and the token scopes, owns whether the run happens at all and what it is permitted to touch. The model owns the triage quality: the label chosen, the duplicate judgement and the tone of the comment are all unverified.
sheets.context_boundary: A fresh, ephemeral context per issue event. The issue title and body, plus whatever repo state the job fetches, cross in; the label and comment API calls cross out. Nothing carries over between runs, so the bot has no memory of a similar issue triaged yesterday unless it re-queries.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts on the issues-opened webhook and ends when the job exits. It stops applying when the workflow is disabled, the branch it lives on changes, or the API credential is revoked.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open and silently from the user's perspective: a failed or skipped job means the issue simply sits untriaged, and nobody notices without alerting on workflow failures. The sharper risk is that issue bodies are attacker-controlled text arriving on a public endpoint, so a crafted issue can try to steer the run; scope the token to labels and comments only, never to code or secrets, and treat the issue text as data. Cost and rate limits also scale with issue volume, including spam.
sheets.version_caveat: This needs credentials in repository secrets and a supported non-interactive auth path (an API key, or a subscription-auth mechanism if the org uses one). The published Claude Code GitHub Action is versioned independently of the CLI and its input names have changed between releases, so pin the action to a tag; I cannot state which tag from model knowledge alone.

scenarios.scenario: Before the agent ends its turn and declares work complete, the test suite must have actually been run and passed during that turn; if not, the agent should be sent back to keep working. This must hold even when the model simply forgets to test.

key.primary: Stop hook that verifies tests ran and passed, and on failure exits 2 (or returns decision "block" with a reason) so Claude must continue working
key.rejected_alternative: A PostToolUse hook on Edit that reminds Claude to run the tests
key.rejection_reason: PostToolUse fires per tool call and cannot gate the end of the turn; it never fires at all when the model declares completion without making another tool call. Stop is the documented event for enforcing validation before accepting a response: its block decision prevents Claude from stopping and feeds the reason back so the conversation continues.
key.lifecycle: Stop event fires when Claude finishes responding; exit code 2 or decision "block" prevents the turn from ending and injects the reason
key.failure_mode: A hook that blocks unconditionally traps the agent in an infinite continue loop; the script needs a termination condition (such as checking the repeat-invocation flag in the hook input) or the session never ends.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook that checks the just-finished turn for real evidence the suite ran and passed (a fresh results artifact it verifies, or the hook running the suite itself) and returns {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."} when that evidence is absent, sending the agent back to work.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A skill or CLAUDE.md rule instructing the model to test before declaring completion. It loses because the stated failure is the model forgetting, and an instruction cannot detect its own omission; only a harness-run gate at turn end can.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness owns the gate, the model owns the remediation. Claude Code refuses to end the turn on the hook's verdict, then the model does the work described in the reason string.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs out of process with stop_hook_active, last_assistant_message, background_tasks and the transcript path on stdin. Only the reason string crosses back into the model's context, and the conversation continues in the same window rather than a fresh one.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires when the main agent has finished responding, once per turn, for the whole session. It does not fire when the stoppage was a user interrupt, and API errors route to StopFailure instead. It stops applying at session end or once the continuation cap trips.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the turn but has a hard escape hatch: Claude Code overrides the hook and ends the turn after 8 consecutive blocks, so a condition that never resolves eventually lets an untested turn through. If the hook infers "tests ran" from a weak proxy such as message text or a stale results file, it either loops until the cap or waves through a false claim. A crashed hook exiting 1 is non-blocking, so a broken gate fails open.
sheets.version_caveat: No version gate on Stop hooks or decision: "block". If the suite runs as a background task, the background_tasks and session_crons arrays that let the hook distinguish "session is done" from "waiting on the test run" are available only in Claude Code v2.1.145 or later; on older versions the hook must infer that state from the transcript.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook, command handler, that checks for evidence of a passing test run in the just-finished turn (a marker file written by a PostToolUse hook on the test command, or a scan of transcript_path) and returns {"decision": "block", "reason": ...} when no such evidence exists. Reserve the milder hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext form for guidance, and use decision block when the gate must read as a failure.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A skill such as a verification-before-completion procedure, which is exactly the advisory shape that fails here: the model must choose to consult and follow it, and the scenario's premise is that it forgets.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code fires Stop when the turn ends and enforces the returned decision, so the model cannot end the turn over the hook's objection.
sheets.context_boundary: The handler runs outside the context window and receives stop_hook_active, last_assistant_message and transcript_path on stdin; the reason string is what crosses back and becomes the model's next instruction inside the same session.
sheets.lifecycle: It runs when the main agent has finished responding, on every turn, and continues to gate turns until the hook is removed. It does not run when the user interrupts, and API failures route to StopFailure instead.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open on handler error, since any exit code other than 2 lets the turn end with a hook-error notice, and a crash is indistinguishable from a deliberate pass. The block is also bounded: after 8 consecutive blocks Claude Code overrides the hook and ends the turn anyway, so a hook that cannot be satisfied degrades to advisory rather than looping forever; guard on stop_hook_active to avoid that path.
sheets.version_caveat: A command Stop hook needs no version gate. The tempting alternative, an agent-type Stop hook that runs the suite itself, is documented as experimental and may change, so it is the wrong choice for a hard gate; the background_tasks and session_crons inputs used to tell "done" from "waiting" need v2.1.145 or later.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook that checks for evidence that the suite ran and passed during this turn, and returns a blocking decision with a reason when it did not, sending the agent back to work. The evidence is produced deterministically by a companion PostToolUse hook that writes a per-session marker (test command, exit code, timestamp) whenever a test command actually executes, so the Stop hook verifies a fact rather than trusting a claim.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A verification skill or a CLAUDE.md checklist telling the agent to run tests before declaring completion, rejected because the stated failure is the model forgetting, and advisory text cannot catch its own omission.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness owns the gate: it will not let the turn end while the hook blocks. The model owns only the remediation, which is to go run the tests.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook executes outside the context window and reads state from disk. What crosses back in is the block reason string, which is injected as the continuation instruction, so the reason text should be short and directive.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires whenever the main agent attempts to end its turn, and it stops blocking as soon as a passing run is recorded for that turn. The marker must be scoped and cleared per turn or the gate goes stale and starts passing on yesterday's green run.
sheets.failure_mode: The characteristic failure is a loop: a hook that blocks unconditionally can pin the agent in a cycle, which is why the payload flag indicating the stop hook is already active must be honoured to break out. It fails open when the evidence check is naive, since running one trivial passing test satisfies a marker that only records that some test command ran. It also adds full-suite latency to every turn boundary, which pushes people to disable it.
sheets.version_caveat: This depends on the Stop hook event supporting a structured blocking decision plus the re-entrancy flag in its payload, and on SubagentStop existing if the same rule must cover subagents. I cannot confirm the exact JSON field names or the minimum version from model knowledge alone. Note also that a user-initiated interrupt does not run the same path, so the gate does not cover an abandoned turn.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook of type "command" that checks for evidence the suite ran and passed during this turn (for example a marker file with the session id and turn timestamp, written by a PostToolUse hook on Bash when the test command exits 0) and returns {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."} when that evidence is absent, so Claude is sent back to keep working.
sheets.rejected_alternative: An agent-type Stop hook that spawns a subagent to run the suite itself. It removes the marker plumbing, but agent hooks are explicitly experimental, cost a model call plus a full test run at every turn end, and return a judgment rather than a recorded exit code.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness owns the outcome: Claude Code decides whether the turn may end, and the model only reacts to the reason string it is handed. The model forgetting to test is precisely what this removes from the model's hands.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook is a subprocess receiving the Stop event JSON (including stop_hook_active and last_assistant_message) on stdin, outside the model's context window. Only the reason string, or hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, crosses back into the conversation, so the turn resumes with a short instruction rather than raw test output unless the hook chooses to include it.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires every time the main agent finishes responding, not only when work is genuinely complete, and applies until the turn is allowed to end. It must read stop_hook_active and exit early when true, or it will keep blocking a condition that will never resolve.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open at the edges: Claude Code overrides the hook after 8 consecutive blocks and ends the turn anyway, Stop hooks do not fire on user interrupts (an API error fires StopFailure instead), and any exit code other than 2 from a crashed script or a missing jq lets the turn finish with only a hook-error notice. It also fires on purely conversational turns, so the check has to tolerate turns where nothing was edited or it becomes noise.
sheets.version_caveat: Stop hooks are generally available and need no flag; raise the eight-block ceiling with the CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP environment variable if convergence legitimately needs more iterations. Agent-type hooks are experimental and may change, and /goal is a built-in session-scoped prompt Stop hook if you want the judgment-based variant without writing configuration.
